## Summary

**Result:** `python reproduce.py` exits `0` with `status: workflow_completed` and a finite aggregate (`[19.5]`), which is also the *scientifically correct* value: the 40 daily values starting 0001-01-01 (year 1 is **not** a leap year; series ends 0001-02-09) all fall within the first `Q-DEC` period, so a single bin with mean 19.5 (sum 780) is exact.

### What I investigated

The task description ("short series fails when aggregated into a coarser bin") suggested a boundary bug in the cftime resample machinery. I audited the full aggregation path — `Dataset.resample` → `CFTimeGrouper.first_items` → `_get_time_bins` → `_get_range_edges`/`_adjust_bin_edges` → `cftime_range` → the `QuarterEnd`/`MonthEnd`/`YearEnd`/`Tick` offset classes in `coding/cftime_offsets.py`, plus the groupby/reduce machinery in `core/groupby.py` and `core/resample.py`.

To determine whether any defect was embedded, I verified the implementation against independent oracles instead of trusting the code:

1. **Pandas parity** (the CFTime code was adapted from pandas): ~10,000 randomized cases spanning every start date, series length (1–800), frequency (`ME`/`MS`/`QS`/`QE`/anchored `Q-DEC`/`QE-MAR`/`YE-MAY`/…), and resample options (`closed`, `label`, `origin={start,start_day,end,end_day,epoch}`, `offset`) — **100% match** (only `loffset`, which pandas 2.3 itself no longer accepts, differed by design).
2. **Calendar oracle** (computed bin labels directly from calendar definitions, independent of xarray code): **68,400 cases** — all 5 calendars (standard, noleap, 360_day, all_leap, julian), quarter-start/quarter-end anchored at 12 months, month/year frequencies, in the era *beyond pandas' datetime64 range* (years 0–4) — **100% match**.
3. **Tick-frequency oracle** (D/h/min/s with all origin modes): all values and totals correct.
